quranVerses.translation: And give good tidings to the patient.
So remember Me; I will remember you.
And He is with you wherever you are.
quranVerses.transliteration: Wa Huwa ma'akum ayna ma kuntum.

quranVerses.arabic: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
quranVerses.translation: Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear.
Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.

quranVerses.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
quranVerses.translation: Indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the good-doers to be lost.

quranVerses.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً
quranVerses.translation: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter.
quranVerses.transliteration: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanah.

quranVerses.translation: Indeed, We have granted you abundant good.

quranVerses.arabic: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مَخْرَجًا
quranVerses.translation: And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out.
quranVerses.transliteration: Wa man yattaqillaha yaj'al lahu makhraja.

quranVerses.arabic: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ
quranVerses.translation: And whoever relies upon Allah — then He is sufficient for him.

quranVerses.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمْ
quranVerses.translation: Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.
quranVerses.transliteration: Innallaha la yughayyiru ma biqawmin hatta yughayyiru ma bi-anfusihim.

quranVerses.translation: And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah.
quranVerses.transliteration: Wasbir wa ma sabruka illa billah.

quranVerses.arabic: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
quranVerses.translation: And that there is nothing for man except that for which he strives.
quranVerses.transliteration: Wa an laysa lil-insani illa ma sa'a.

quranVerses.translation: So indeed, with hardship comes ease.
And He is the Forgiving, the Loving.
Say: He is Allah, the One.

hadithQuotes.text: The best among you are those who have the best manners and character.
None of you truly believes until he wishes for his brother what he wishes for himself.
The strong person is not the one who overcomes others by strength, but the one who controls himself while in anger.
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.
Make things easy and do not make them difficult, cheer people up and do not make them run away.
The most beloved of deeds to Allah are those that are consistent, even if small.

dailyDuas.translation: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.

dailyDuas.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
dailyDuas.translation: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.

dailyDuas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَعِنِّي عَلَى ذِكْرِكَ وَشُكْرِكَ وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ
dailyDuas.translation: O Allah, help me remember You, thank You, and worship You in the best way.
Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.
O Allah, I ask You for well-being.

lifeStages.label: Born
lifeStages.note: A single breath, and a whole life begins.

lifeStages.label: Return
lifeStages.note: Every soul shall taste death — Surah Al-Imran 3:185.

prophetsJourney.name: Adam
prophetsJourney.topic: The first human — creation, trial, and repentance.
prophetsJourney.summary: The first human being created by Allah, and the first prophet. He and Hawwa (Eve) were placed in Paradise, then sent to Earth after a moment of forgetfulness. His story sets the pattern for every human struggle: temptation, error, and the mercy of returning to Allah.

prophetsJourney.name: Idris
prophetsJourney.topic: Knowledge, patience, and righteousness.
prophetsJourney.summary: An early prophet praised in the Qur'an for his truthfulness and elevated status. Little detail is given about his life, but he's remembered as a model of patience, knowledge, and devotion long before later, better-known prophets.

prophetsJourney.name: Nuh (Noah)
prophetsJourney.topic: Nearly a thousand years of patient calling; the Great Flood.
prophetsJourney.summary: Called his people to monotheism for close to a thousand years, facing mockery and rejection almost the entire time. When they refused to listen, Allah commanded him to build an ark, and a great flood saved the believers while punishing the rest.

prophetsJourney.name: Hud
prophetsJourney.topic: Warned his people against arrogance and idolatry.
prophetsJourney.summary: Sent to the people of 'Ad, a powerful civilization known for their impressive architecture and physical strength. He warned them against arrogance and idol worship, but they dismissed him — until a devastating windstorm proved his warning true.

prophetsJourney.name: Salih
prophetsJourney.topic: The miracle of the she-camel; a call to humility.
prophetsJourney.summary: Sent to the people of Thamud, who were given a miraculous she-camel as a sign from Allah. When they killed the camel out of arrogance and defiance, a swift punishment followed, standing as a lesson in humility and respecting divine signs.

prophetsJourney.name: Ibrahim (Abraham)
prophetsJourney.topic: Monotheism, sacrifice, and being called 'Khalilullah' — the friend of Allah.
prophetsJourney.summary: Known as 'Khalilullah', the friend of Allah. He broke his people's idols, survived being thrown into a fire, and was tested with the near-sacrifice of his son — becoming the father of monotheism for many nations that followed.

prophetsJourney.name: Lut (Lot)
prophetsJourney.topic: A warning against immorality and injustice.
prophetsJourney.summary: A nephew of Ibrahim sent to a town steeped in immorality and injustice. Despite his warnings, the people persisted, and the town was ultimately destroyed while Lut and his believing family were saved.

prophetsJourney.name: Ismail (Ishmael)
prophetsJourney.topic: Obedience and patience at the edge of sacrifice.
prophetsJourney.summary: The son who calmly accepted being offered as a sacrifice in obedience to Allah's command, only for Allah to replace him with a ram at the last moment. His trust and patience are commemorated every year during Eid al-Adha.

prophetsJourney.name: Ishaq (Isaac)
prophetsJourney.topic: Continuation of the covenant of prophethood.
prophetsJourney.summary: Ibrahim's second son, through whom prophethood continued into later generations. His life is closely tied to the broader story of his father and the covenant passed down through his own children.

prophetsJourney.name: Yaqub (Jacob)
prophetsJourney.topic: Patience through decades of loss and hope.
prophetsJourney.summary: Endured decades of grief after losing his beloved son Yusuf, never giving up hope of being reunited with him. His patience through prolonged sorrow is held up as a model of quiet, enduring faith.

prophetsJourney.name: Yusuf (Joseph)
prophetsJourney.topic: Betrayal, trial, and forgiveness — the best of stories.
prophetsJourney.summary: Betrayed by his own brothers, sold into slavery, and imprisoned on a false accusation — yet he rose to a position of power in Egypt and forgave everyone who wronged him. His story is called the most detailed and instructive in the Qur'an.

prophetsJourney.name: Ayyub (Job)
prophetsJourney.topic: Patience in prolonged suffering and illness.
prophetsJourney.summary: Lost his wealth, his health, and his children, yet never stopped praising Allah. His patience through extreme, prolonged suffering has made his name synonymous with steadfastness in hardship.

prophetsJourney.name: Shuayb
prophetsJourney.topic: Honesty in trade and dealing justly with people.
prophetsJourney.summary: Sent to a community notorious for cheating in trade and dealing dishonestly. He called them to fairness in business and worship of Allah alone, warning that no amount of profit is worth built on dishonesty.

prophetsJourney.name: Musa (Moses)
prophetsJourney.topic: Liberation, the Torah, and direct conversation with Allah.
prophetsJourney.summary: Raised in Pharaoh's own palace, then called by Allah at Mount Sinai to free the Israelites from slavery. His confrontations with Pharaoh, the parting of the sea, and receiving the Torah make his story the most repeated in the Qur'an.

prophetsJourney.name: Harun (Aaron)
prophetsJourney.topic: Support, eloquence, and standing beside his brother.
prophetsJourney.summary: Musa's brother and closest support, gifted with eloquence to help carry the message. He stood beside Musa through the hardest confrontations, a reminder that even prophets needed people they could lean on.

prophetsJourney.name: Dawud (David)
prophetsJourney.topic: Justice, the Psalms, and a grateful heart.
prophetsJourney.summary: A king known for his justice, beautiful recitation of the Psalms (Zabur), and remarkable gratitude despite ruling over a vast kingdom. He balanced worldly power with constant remembrance of Allah.

prophetsJourney.name: Sulaiman (Solomon)
prophetsJourney.topic: Wisdom, vast dominion, and humility in gratitude.
prophetsJourney.summary: Inherited his father Dawud's kingdom and was given authority over jinn, animals, and the wind, along with immense wealth. Despite this, he remained humble, always attributing his blessings back to Allah's favor.

prophetsJourney.name: Ilyas (Elijah)
prophetsJourney.topic: Calling his people away from idol worship.
prophetsJourney.summary: Called his people away from worshipping an idol back to the worship of Allah alone. He faced fierce resistance from a society deeply attached to its false gods, staying firm in his message regardless.

prophetsJourney.name: Al-Yasa (Elisha)
prophetsJourney.topic: Continuing the guidance after Ilyas.
prophetsJourney.summary: Continued the mission after Ilyas, carrying the same call to his community. The Qur'an lists him among the righteous, though it shares few specific details of his life.

prophetsJourney.name: Yunus (Jonah)
prophetsJourney.topic: Repentance from within the belly of the whale.
prophetsJourney.summary: Left his people in frustration without Allah's permission and ended up swallowed by a whale. His prayer of repentance from within its belly is one of the most quoted verses on turning back to Allah in distress.

prophetsJourney.name: Zakariya (Zechariah)
prophetsJourney.topic: A prayer for righteous offspring, answered in old age.
prophetsJourney.summary: Prayed for a righteous child late into old age, when it seemed biologically impossible. Allah answered with Yahya, a lesson in never underestimating the power of a sincere, persistent prayer.

prophetsJourney.name: Yahya (John)
prophetsJourney.topic: Purity and righteousness from childhood.
prophetsJourney.summary: Given wisdom and purity from a very young age, living a life devoted entirely to worship and guidance. He's remembered for his integrity and the seriousness with which he approached his mission from childhood.

prophetsJourney.name: Isa (Jesus)
prophetsJourney.topic: Miracles, compassion, and calling to worship Allah alone.
prophetsJourney.summary: Born miraculously to Maryam without a father, and given the ability to perform miracles by Allah's permission. He called his people to worship Allah alone, and the Qur'an describes him with deep honor while rejecting claims of divinity.

prophetsJourney.name: Muhammad ﷺ
prophetsJourney.topic: The seal of the prophets — mercy to all of creation.
prophetsJourney.summary: The final messenger, sent as a mercy to all of creation. His life — from an orphaned childhood in Makkah to receiving the Qur'an and establishing a community built on justice and compassion — completes and confirms the message of every prophet before him.

islamicCalendar.name: Ramadan
islamicCalendar.note: A month of fasting, increased prayer, and Qur'an recitation.

islamicCalendar.name: Eid al-Fitr
islamicCalendar.note: Marks the end of Ramadan — a day of gratitude and celebration.

islamicCalendar.name: Eid al-Adha
islamicCalendar.note: Commemorates Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice, marked by Hajj.

islamicCalendar.name: Ashura
islamicCalendar.note: A recommended day of fasting, rich with historical significance.

islamicCalendar.name: Mawlid al-Nabi
islamicCalendar.note: Commemorates the birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
